newsitem.title: USA: Columbus council approves cleanup near arena site.
newsitem.headline: Columbus council approves cleanup near arena site.

text.p: Columbus City Council has approved a $2.7 million contract for underground cleanup at a site slated for surface parking adjacent to its planned sports arena development, city Finance Director Wyatt Kingseed said Tuesday.
Columbus officials anticipate spending less than $12 million preparing the former Ohio Penitentiary site for the arena-related development Kingseed said.
After its initial use as surface parking, the city anticipates commercial development on the site by one of the future owners of the privately financed arena, Kingseed said.
All but five of the structures on the site have been razed and abatement of above ground contaminants has been completed, Kingseed said.
Nationwide Insurance Co and Dispatch Printing Co plan a $125 million arena to house a National Hockey League expansion franchise scheduled to begin play in the 2000-2001 season.
Nationwide will provide 90 percent of the financing and the Dispatch 10 percent for the arena while Columbus and Franklin County have agreed to meet infrastructure needs.
Columbus issued $8.1 million of bonds for the arena project last December and "with luck" will not have to issue more debt for this phase of the project, Kingseed said.
Contracts for the infrastructure work to date total about $8 million, Kingseed said.
Discussions continue on the lease arrangements for the facility and possible future demolition and water and sewer improvements could increase the city costs, Kingseed said.
